JV: A joint venture with another contract holder. Review the contract interest and fee split with title before introducing a buyer.
ARV: After-repair value: what the repaired property may sell for, supported by comparable sales. An estimate or a seller's claim is not verified value.
MAO: Maximum allowable offer, calculated from supported value, repairs and your fee. A buyer ceiling is not your seller offer.
Comps: Different, comparable properties with recorded sale details and source links. Missing facts or off-grid properties do not qualify.
Verified: Value supported by at least three qualifying real sold comparables. This does not verify title, repairs or ownership.
Preliminary: Value supported by two qualifying sold comparables. It remains preliminary, not a final offer.
Texas list-price: A sold home's last advertised price, not its hidden sale price. This tier is preliminary market support and never verified sold value.
Assignment: Transfer of an assignable purchase contract interest. Title and counsel must confirm the contract and local requirements.
Double close: Two separate closings: purchase and resale. Funding, timing and costs must be arranged with title.
EMD: Earnest-money deposit held by the agreed title or escrow company. A promise of payment is not a received deposit.
Subject-to: Taking a property subject to an existing loan. The loan, consent issues and legal risks require professional review.
Seller financing: The seller accepts payments under agreed loan terms instead of receiving the entire price at closing.
Novation: A replacement agreement involving the relevant parties. It is not automatically the same as assigning a contract.
Section 8 rent: Housing-voucher payment context, not guaranteed rent. Local program rules, property approval and the lease matter.
Lane: The work a record currently needs: an active deal, a status check, more evidence or a blocked item. Records are kept, not erased.
Verdict: GOOD fits a recorded buyer ceiling; POSSIBLE needs evidence or negotiation; OVERPRICED exceeds the ceiling; STALE passed its deadline; NO was rejected or ended.
JV status: A recorded step from Found through Vetted, holder and contract checks, signed JV, buyer deposit and Closed. Expired and Dead stay in history.
Approval: An operator's recorded review decision. Pending imports cannot introduce a buyer or prove a value by themselves.
Buy box: The buyer's stated locations, property types, budget and other purchase criteria. Missing criteria are not invented.
Spread: An estimated difference between the buyer ceiling and asking, adjusted for the recorded JV split. It is not guaranteed profit or a closing payment.
Title company: The closing provider that checks title and handles settlement. A listed company has not automatically approved your deal.
Flood zone X: A mapped lower-risk flood designation, not a promise that flooding cannot occur. Check current mapping and insurance requirements.
After the sale: A notice's sale date passed. The outcome and current owner still need source evidence before treating it as an active opportunity.
Today’s Deals: Submitted deals awaiting review and checked deals worth considering today. The daily target is not a promise of automatic acquisition.
Buyer max: A derived ceiling from the buyer's explicitly recorded budget or percentage rule. It is not an offer or a commitment from the buyer.
Deadline: The stated closing or auction date. An unknown date stays unknown; an expired deal is retained for history.
Captured: When the source was recorded. This is not automatically when the deal was posted or when its sale takes place.
Daily target: Ten vetted deals is the goal. The count shows actual reviewed evidence, not generated or promised deals.
Import: Preview submitted records, then explicitly save them. Deal imports remain pending even if buyer bulk approval is selected.
Recheck: Record a new human source check today. Loading this screen never asserts that the holder was contacted or the deal is available.
Contract checks: Record the actual contract, signatures, assignment rights, closing date, title provider and matching owner evidence. Checking a box is a human assertion.
Copy message: Copies a draft for your review. The application does not send it or record a contact attempt.
Leads: Stored seller records and source evidence. A saved record count is not the count of workable or callable properties.
Buyers found: Source-backed buyer candidates with approval decisions. A public post is not a purchase commitment.
Open source: Opens the recorded source in your browser. The server does not fetch listing or people-search sites.
Filters: Narrow this list by state, county or city. Filtering never changes the saved record.
Help: Plain-English definitions for the dashboard. They explain terms, not legal or financial advice.
